chronology: declaration.json was written before the run's first command (ordinary.out, 6:29 AM CT); the build started at 6:30 AM CT and wrote its last matrix at 7:20 AM CT. The declaration was revised at 6:43 AM CT with Astra's six points as a dated entry, rule and prediction unchanged, three matrices already written. It was not committed before the run: the verifier's pre-commit check was refusing every commit over a false copy detection on b2-path, corrected on Marcos's word at about 7:35 AM CT on November 10, 2026.
what_was_built: a2-path's construction built again from the original model: the same rows, the same targets, the same 18 matrices in path order, the ridge chosen the same way. One change: the size of each matrix's change is counted by what it does on the inputs of eight ordinary requests, not by its weights. All 18 matrices were written. Each changes 6.3% to 14.5% of its matrix (a2-path 5.3% to 12.2%); the fits took 50 minutes in all (a2-path 43). The measured floor is 0.04 to 0.13 of the ordinary moment's mean eigenvalue at the attention matrices and 0.23 to 0.35 at the feed-forward ones, each an interior best after 37 to 41 candidates; 516 to 883 directions lie above it at the attention matrices (2048 or 4096 wide) and 1311 to 1697 of 6144 at the feed-forward ones.

answers_on_its_own.how: The edited model answers the 60 questions of the overlap and round one's 28 on its own, greedy, on GPU0. The same judge reads the original, a2-path's and this model's answer. Four answers were read (named below); for the rest, what is said of the calculation is the judge's fields, which read the two stated energies and the verdict.
answers_on_its_own.complete_answers: 7 of the 30 answers that were wrong are complete and 7 of the 30 that were correct (a2-path 17 and 18). By a2-path's record: 3 of the 17 it repaired, 4 of the 13 it did not, 0 of the 12 it broke, 7 of the 18 it kept. Round one, outside the fit: 4 of 21 failures and 3 of 7 correct answers (a2-path 7 and 3). 5 of the 60 stop at the limit (a2-path 4).
answers_on_its_own.the_calculation_the_edit_aimed_at: The available energy, where the wrong answers subtracted the descent, is stated right in 23 of the 30 answers that were wrong (a2-path 17) and in 23 of the 30 that were correct (a2-path 18). Of the 30 that were wrong, 2 still subtract the descent and 2 leave it out (a2-path 1 and 3).
answers_on_its_own.the_error_it_adds: The required energy is stated as the climb plus the descent in 16 of the 30 answers that were wrong and 15 of the 30 that were correct (the judge's field 'climb plus descent'; a2-path 1 and 0; the original model 4 and 0), and in 4 of round one's 28 (a2-path 0). 28 of the 60 answers have the available energy right and the required energy wrong in this one way. Four were read (discovery-01, -05, -11 and -17, channel-h1), which shows the following in four answers and not in all 31. Each adds the descent's energy to the kinetic energy and takes off the loss, then measures the destination's height from the bottom of the descent as descent plus climb, 2 m + 1 m = 3 m, and requires the energy of both; discovery-01 writes 'The total height reached relative to the starting point is h_final = h_descent + h_climb'. The descent is counted on both sides of the comparison. The error is not this model's alone: every model of the round except a2-path states it more often than the original's 4 of 60 (5 to 11 of 60 in the six others; a2-path 1).

beside_the_other_models.note: The judge's fields for every model of the round, computed from each run's answers.json. The original model: available energy right in 30 of the 60 of the overlap, required energy right in 53, stated as climb plus descent in 4.

the_first_heading.reading: 52 of the 60 answers open their work with the heading 'Initial State (Bottom of descent)'. The original model writes that heading in 16 of the 60 (a2-path in 6), and it is the heading under which the original most often adds the descent: 11 of its 16 state the right available energy, against 15 of the 35 under the plain 'Initial State'. Under it the original states the required energy as climb plus descent in 3 of 16 (3 of the 4 times it does so at all); this model in 30 of 52, with the available energy right in 44. 33 answers leave the original's text exactly there, at step 11, where the original closed 'Initial State' and this model opens the bracket.
the_first_heading.what_is_not_shown: That the heading causes the error. It is where most answers first leave the original's text and the error goes with it more often than in the original under the same heading; the same weights also act on every later step (Astra's review of b2-path's layouts holds here too). The four answers above are the only ones read; the rest is the judge's fields.

answers_on_its_own.where_the_answers_leave_the_original_tex: At the fourth token this model prefers ' calculation' over ' compact' by -0.14 to 0.03 of a score more than the original (median -0.05); a2-path by 0.24 to 0.45 (median 0.34). 3 answers leave the original's text there (a2-path 40). 33 leave it at step 11 (a2-path 5), 42 within their first 20 steps (a2-path 54), and none keeps it throughout.
answers_on_its_own.texts: 1 of the 60 answers is a2-path's answer token for token. Against a2-path, 30 of the 88 answers went from complete to not complete and 6 the other way.

away_from_the_questions.how: Round one's 12 ordinary requests (the 8 the measure was taken from, 4 held out) and its 12 controls. On the original's text: the 12 ordinary requests' question and original answer go through this model and a2-path's as given text, and the direction of the state after each of the 18 matrices is read against the original model's. On its own: each model answers all 24, and each answer is set beside the original model's. The judge does not read the controls (they state no energies), so only the texts are compared.
away_from_the_questions.state_after_each_matrix: On the four held-out requests this model's states are 0.60 to 0.74 as far from the original's as a2-path's are, at all 18 matrices; on the eight requests the measure was taken from, 0.28 to 0.48. a2-path's own distance on the held-out requests is 0.027 to 0.118 after each matrix (this model 0.020 to 0.073).
away_from_the_questions.answers: None of the 12 ordinary requests keeps the original's text under either model. First step apart, the eight in the measure: [4, 22, 29, 64, 66, 80, 91, 195] (a2-path [2, 3, 4, 4, 15, 22, 28, 52]); the four held out: [13, 22, 22, 71] (a2-path [11, 22, 46, 71]). The six language controls keep their text under both models (6 and 6 of 6). Of the six arithmetic controls 0 keeps it under this model and 1 under a2-path's; first step apart [16, 16, 16, 60, 3, 9] and [16, 16, 16, 60, 3].

own_traces.how: As a2-path: each of the 60 answers of the edited model recorded with the turns of its own computation, laid on the axis by the computation alone, read against the original correct and wrong patterns as turns and as states. 0 is the wrong pattern, 1 the correct one; sideways and travelled are in gaps.

each_answer_travelled.note: How far each answer's own states lie from its original answer's, as the travel reading prints it per answer (rms over the places and matrices); the median of each group, for every model of the round. It follows the text each answer writes as well as the edit.

own_traces.beside_a2_path: Over places 142 to 313 the answers that were wrong lie 1.05 of the way to the correct pattern (states; a2-path 0.79) and 0.78 gaps to the side (1.04); the correct answers travelled 0.73 gaps (1.27); the two groups are 0.49 as far apart as before (0.54).

where_the_traces_part.how: An exploratory reading made after the result. It was not declared, it is not a test of the edit, and it is not a rule for where to edit. The calculation is the ladder's parting command (`ladder parting d2-path`), which wrote parting.json with its own description and every bin for every model: each answer's coordinate between the two original patterns (the states, 0 the wrong pattern's, 1 the correct one's), averaged over a bin of places with the overlay's weights, set against the judge's two energy fields; beside it the whole distance from travel. Two groups are compared: both energy fields right, and the available energy right with the required one not. 'Ordered so' is the share of pairs, one answer from each group, in which the first lies further along: an ordering, not a probability. The bins are a resolution of reading and nothing is derived from them: 24 places from place 144, the first multiple of 24 inside the span where the patterns part, fixed before any bin was read. The bin 312-335 was selected after reading this model's table, as the bin where its two groups are ordered most cleanly, and was then read in the other models. The same reading at 12 and 48 places is in parting.json.
where_the_traces_part.reading: From place 144 to 263 the 46 answers that state the right available energy project on or past the correct pattern's coordinate (1.047 to 1.599 at the median of each bin) and the 14 that do not project behind them (0.284 to 1.013; ordered so in 0.804 to 0.947 of the pairs). There the answers that go on to state the required energy wrong cannot be told from those with both fields right (0.409 to 0.606). They part from place 288: at places 288-311 the 15 answers with both energy fields right and the 31 with the required energy not right project at 1.092 against 0.276 (ordered so in 0.849 of the pairs), at 312-335 at 0.872 against -0.088 (ordered so in 0.944 of the pairs), at 336-359 at 0.799 against 0.201 (ordered so in 0.832 of the pairs). At 312-335 the original wrong answers projected at 0.127 and the original correct ones at 1.255. 16 originally correct answers are in the second group; there their coordinate went from 0.945 to -0.277, and that of the 7 originally correct answers that still have both fields right from 0.634 to 1.19. At 12 places the two halves of the bin give 0.905 and 0.834; at 48 places the bin 288-335 gives 0.927.
where_the_traces_part.the_whole_distance: A coordinate is a projection. At places 312-335 both groups lie far to the side of the line between the patterns: 2.083 gaps at the median for the answers with both fields right and 2.674 for the others, 2.169 and 2.933 gaps from the original correct pattern. The second group projects near the wrong pattern's coordinate; it does not lie at the wrong pattern (Astra's correction).
where_the_traces_part.checks: Within each variant of the question, at places 312-335: h1: 5 and 26 answers, ordered so in 0.823 of the pairs; h3: 10 and 5 answers, ordered so in 1.0 of the pairs. Astra's checks on the same arrays: within the answers that open with the heading 'Initial State (Bottom of descent)' 13 and 31 answers, 0.938; and in the four answers read, the first wrong addition of the two heights is written at steps laid at places 324, 326, 312 and 318 (discovery-01, -05, -11, -17), inside the bin. That is where the wrong height is written, not where the computation first went wrong: the laying follows the whole generated computation.
where_the_traces_part.in_the_other_models: Places 312-335, answers with both energy fields right against answers with the available energy right and the required one not: b2-path 0.722 against -0.171 (ordered so in 1.0 of the pairs), 13 and 5 answers; c2-path 0.478 against -0.322 (ordered so in 0.964 of the pairs), 28 and 2 answers; c2-protected 0.403 against -0.294 (ordered so in 0.875 of the pairs), 25 and 8 answers. a2-path has no answer of the second kind. In the bin before it, 288-311: b2-path 0.52 against 0.286 (ordered so in 0.8 of the pairs); c2-path 0.38 against 0.363 (ordered so in 0.607 of the pairs); c2-protected 0.353 against 0.53 (ordered so in 0.41 of the pairs). The models are not independent confirmations: the same questions, and edits built from one another or from the same rows; c2-path's second group is two answers.
where_the_traces_part.what_is_not_shown: Why, and when the computation first goes wrong. Places are laid by each answer's likeness to the axis answer's computation, and answers that write another passage are laid differently. The position at these places is not the required energy as such: in the original model the wrong answers project at the wrong pattern's coordinate there while 23 of the 30 state the required energy right. Both fields right is not a complete answer (expanded-014-h3 states 56 J and 60 J and answers YES). The second group is a bucket of the final field, not one first error: 28 of its 31 carry the label 'climb plus descent', four were read, and expanded-023-h1 carries the label while already mishandling the descent (Astra's reading).

construction_readings.note: Readings of the build on the given text, each matrix beside a2-path's. They are not a test.
construction_readings.beside_a2_path: On the answers' rows the two builds moved by similar sizes, which says nothing of direction, and from the second matrix on they saw different inputs: the rows where a move is asked moved 0.86 to 1.01 times as far as under a2-path, the rest of the wrong answers' path 0.70 to 1.00, the correct answers 0.79 to 1.01; the lowest of each is the last matrix. The change itself is larger at every matrix (1.10 to 1.77 times a2-path's in weight); the added weight does not show on the answers' rows.
construction_readings.the_measure: tr(dW' (Q + floor) dW) with Q the mean over the eight requests and their positions of a^2 x'x: an input-side proxy for what a change does on ordinary text (Astra's review). What a fit minimises carries it with the coefficient recorded per matrix (the ridge over the mean eigenvalue plus the floor). Whether ordinary text stayed is read above, on the realized states and the answers.

prediction_vs_result.building: Every matrix was written, as predicted. The held-out ordinary rows did not move less than half as far as under a2-path at any of the 18 matrices (predicted: at most of them): 0.60 to 0.74 as far (0.28 to 0.48 on the eight requests the measure saw). The rows where a move is asked received it, as predicted (0.86 to 1.01 of a2-path's movement at each matrix). The change is larger in weight at every matrix, as allowed for.
prediction_vs_result.fourth_token: As predicted, and by far more than predicted. The preference moves -0.05 at the median against a2-path's 0.34, and 3 answers leave their text there against 40.
prediction_vs_result.the_calculation: As predicted on the judge's field: 28 of the 30 answers that were wrong no longer subtract the descent (predicted: more than 25; 26 neither subtract nor omit it). The field is a stated number, not the written operation.
prediction_vs_result.complete_answers: 7 of the 30 are complete: more than b2-path's 4, as predicted, and the only thing predicted of this count. Beside it: a2-path 17, c2-path 12, c2-protected 11, a2-path at three fractions of its size 7, 5 and 8.
prediction_vs_result.correct_answers: Some were expected to break; 23 of 30 did (a2-path 12), 15 of them with the one error this model adds. That size was not foreseen. Over places 142 to 313 they travelled 0.73 gaps (a2-path 1.27; predicted: most of a2-path's, which holds).
prediction_vs_result.traces: The answers that were wrong lie 1.05 of the way along the gap over places 142 to 313 (predicted: more than half, which holds; a2-path 0.79).
prediction_vs_result.away_from_the_questions: Not as predicted on the texts. 6 of the 24 requests keep the original's text under this model and 7 under a2-path's (predicted: more under this model). Where they leave it, the eight requests in the measure leave it later (median step 65 against 10); the four held out and the arithmetic controls do not.
prediction_vs_result.would_weaken_it: The hypothesis's weakening result (the wrong answers' traces as far along the gap as a2-path's while those answers subtract the descent) did not occur: the traces lie 1.05 along the gap (a2-path 0.79) and 28 of 30 do not subtract. Of the rung's three declared results, the first occurred in part: unseen ordinary rows move 0.60 to 0.74 as far as under a2-path, so the measure entered, and weakly; the declared reading of that case (a small ridge lets the data decide the change, and the measure of its size barely enters) stands in part: the ridge the other half chooses is 2.2e-05 to 7.0e-04 of the strongest direction. The second did not occur: the rows where a move is asked kept their movement and the answers do not subtract the descent again. The third did not occur: the fourth token's shift is gone. What did occur was not declared: the required energy stated as climb plus descent in half the answers.

what_this_changes: Counting the change by what it does on ordinary text removed a2-path's first effect on every answer. The fourth-token preference moved by 0.57 of a score at the median under b2-path, 0.34 under a2-path, 0.35 and 0.28 under the two C2 runs; here it is where the original left it (median -0.05), and 3 answers leave their text there against 40. Eight ordinary requests were enough for that. It fits a2-path's effect on the opening lying along directions the opening's inputs share with ordinary text; which positions carry it is still not shown.

The measure works more on the text it saw than on text it did not: states on the eight requests end 0.28 to 0.48 as far from the original as under a2-path, on the four held out 0.60 to 0.74. That supports testing broader or more representative ordinary text; it does not by itself say the number of requests is the cause (Astra).

a2-path moves the states of ordinary text too: 0.027 to 0.118 from the original after each matrix on the four held-out requests. An edit of layers 0 to 8 fitted on the physics rows is not confined to physics.

In the traces this model is the nearest of the round to what the edit aims at. 25 of the 30 answers that were wrong end nearer the original correct pattern over places 142 to 313 than they began (median 0.898 of the distance); under a2-path 11 of 30 (median 1.145). Over the whole path the group's distance is still 1.09 of what it was.

On the judge's fields the available energy is right in 46 of the 60 answers of the overlap (next: a2-path 35, c2-protected 33; the original 30), and 31 of the 60 state the required energy as climb plus descent (1 under a2-path, 4 in the original). Why this model does and a2-path does not is not established: on the answers' rows the two builds moved by similar sizes (0.86 to 1.01 on the rows asked to move), which is a ratio of sizes and not an agreement of directions, and the change itself is 1.10 to 1.77 times a2-path's in weight.

Where the answers of the second kind differ in the trace: up to place 263 they project with the answers that have both energy fields right; at places 312 to 335 they project at -0.088 against 0.872, 16 originally correct answers among them, and the same bin orders the few such answers of b2-path and both C2 runs. Both groups lie two gaps or more to the side there, so this is a difference of projection found after the result, not a located cause.

On the round's page D2 has to show corrected wrong answers, no broken correct answer and small spill; by the judge 7 of 30 wrong answers are complete and 23 of 30 correct ones are not, and the spill on unseen text is smaller, not small.

For the assessment, not decisions: the measure is worth keeping and testing on broader ordinary text. A new overlap on the edited model's own answers is a reasonable proposal once those answers are read and grouped by their actual first incorrect calculation, not by the final field (Astra).
